topic: Days' supply: insulin pens, inhalers, eye drops (20 gtt/mL)
front: Calc: insulin glargine 100 units/mL, five 3 mL pens; 30 units daily plus a 2-unit prime each injection. Days' supply?

bullets.trap: Forgetting the prime overstates supply (50 days).

back: 46 days. Given: 5 × 3 mL × 100 units = 1,500 units. Work: 30 + 2 prime = 32 units/day; 1,500 ÷ 32 = 46.9 → 46 days. Exam trap: Forgetting the prime overstates supply (50 days).

source.recommendation: Insulin glargine labeling: 100 units/mL, 3 mL prefilled pens; perform a safety test (prime, typically 2 units) before each injection. Days' supply = total units ÷ units used per day, rounded down.

front: Calc: 20 kg child, amoxicillin 90 mg/kg/day divided BID, 400 mg/5 mL. Volume per dose?

bullets.trap: mg/kg/day is the daily total; divide before converting to mL.

back: 11.25 mL twice daily. Given: 90 × 20 = 1,800 mg/day; 900 mg per dose. Work: 900 mg ÷ 400 mg × 5 mL = 11.25 mL BID. Exam trap: mg/kg/day is the daily total; divide before converting to mL.

source.recommendation: AAP 2013 AOM: high-dose amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. Dose per administration = daily dose ÷ number of doses; volume = dose ÷ concentration.

front: Calc: 100 kg patient with DVT, CrCl 25 mL/min. Enoxaparin treatment dose?

bullets.treat: CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg once daily = 100 mg daily. Prophylaxis drops 40 to 30 mg daily.
bullets.trap: Don't just halve each q12h dose; change the interval.

back: 100 mg SC once daily. Given: Usual treatment: 1 mg/kg every 12 hours. Work: CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg once daily = 100 mg daily. Prophylaxis drops 40 to 30 mg daily. Exam trap: Don't just halve each q12h dose; change the interval.

source.recommendation: Enoxaparin labeling: DVT treatment 1 mg/kg SC q12h (or 1.5 mg/kg daily for selected inpatients); CrCl <30 mL/min: treatment 1 mg/kg SC once daily, prophylaxis 30 mg once daily. CHEST 2021 VTE guideline supports LMWH as an anticoagulant option.

topic: IV infusion rate: mL/h and gtt/min with drop factor
front: Calc: 1,000 mL over 8 hours with a 15 gtt/mL set. mL/h and gtt/min?

bullets.clue: Rate = volume ÷ time; gtt/min = mL/h × drop factor ÷ 60.
bullets.trap: Microdrip sets are 60 gtt/mL: then gtt/min equals mL/h.

back: 125 mL/h; 31 gtt/min. Given: Rate = volume ÷ time; gtt/min = mL/h × drop factor ÷ 60. Work: 1,000 ÷ 8 = 125 mL/h; 125 × 15 ÷ 60 = 31.25 → 31 gtt/min. Exam trap: Microdrip sets are 60 gtt/mL: then gtt/min equals mL/h.

source.recommendation: USP <1160> Pharmaceutical Calculations in Pharmacy Practice includes IV flow-rate calculations: mL/h = total volume ÷ hours; drops/min = (mL/h × drop factor) ÷ 60.

front: Calc: norepinephrine 4 mg in 250 mL; 80 kg patient at 0.1 mcg/kg/min. Pump rate?

bullets.trap: Convert mg to mcg and minutes to hours before dividing.

back: 30 mL/h. Given: Concentration = 4,000 mcg ÷ 250 mL = 16 mcg/mL. Work: 0.1 × 80 = 8 mcg/min × 60 = 480 mcg/h; 480 ÷ 16 = 30 mL/h. Exam trap: Convert mg to mcg and minutes to hours before dividing.

diagram.alt: Drip rate calculation: concentration 4 mg in 250 mL is 16 mcg/mL; dose 0.1 mcg/kg/min times 80 kg is 8 mcg/min, times 60 is 480 mcg/h; divided by 16 gives 30 mL/h.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: infusion rate calculations. mL/h = (dose mcg/kg/min × weight kg × 60) ÷ concentration mcg/mL. Norepinephrine 4 mg/250 mL = 16 mcg/mL per labeling dilution.

front: Calc: 90 kg patient starting the weight-based heparin nomogram for VTE; 25,000 units/500 mL. Bolus and rate?

bullets.trap: Titrate to your lab's aPTT or anti-Xa range, not a fixed number.

back: Bolus 7,200 units; 1,620 units/h = 32.4 mL/h. Given: Raschke: 80 units/kg bolus, then 18 units/kg/h. Work: 80 × 90 = 7,200; 18 × 90 = 1,620 units/h ÷ 50 units/mL = 32.4 mL/h. Exam trap: Titrate to your lab's aPTT or anti-Xa range, not a fixed number.

source.recommendation: Raschke RA et al. Ann Intern Med 1993 weight-based nomogram: 80 units/kg bolus, 18 units/kg/h infusion, adjusted by aPTT. Target ranges are institution-specific (calibrated aPTT or anti-Xa).

topic: Opioid conversion with MME and cross-tolerance reduction
front: Calc: oxycodone 30 mg every 6 hours. Total MME, and what if switching to morphine?

bullets.treat: 120 × 1.5 = 180 MME. For a switch, reduce the new opioid 25–50% for incomplete cross-tolerance.
bullets.trap: CDC: MME factors estimate overdose risk; they aren't a dosing conversion table. Methadone is nonlinear.

back: 180 MME/day. Given: CDC factor: oxycodone 1.5. 30 × 4 = 120 mg/day. Work: 120 × 1.5 = 180 MME. For a switch, reduce the new opioid 25–50% for incomplete cross-tolerance. Exam trap: CDC: MME factors estimate overdose risk; they aren't a dosing conversion table. Methadone is nonlinear.

source.recommendation: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain 2022: conversion factors (oxycodone 1.5, hydrocodone 1, morphine 1, hydromorphone 5) estimate MME; they are not intended as dose-conversion tables; when switching opioids, reduce for incomplete cross-tolerance; methadone conversion is nonlinear. Use lowest effective dose and reassess before increasing.

front: Calc: prednisone 40 mg daily needs to become dexamethasone. Equivalent dose?

bullets.clue: Equivalents: hydrocortisone 20 = prednisone 5 = methylprednisolone 4 = dexamethasone 0.75 mg.
bullets.trap: Dexamethasone has no mineralocorticoid effect; hydrocortisone does.

back: Dexamethasone 6 mg. Given: Equivalents: hydrocortisone 20 = prednisone 5 = methylprednisolone 4 = dexamethasone 0.75 mg. Work: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 units × 0.75 = 6 mg. Exam trap: Dexamethasone has no mineralocorticoid effect; hydrocortisone does.

source.recommendation: Standard glucocorticoid equivalence (anti-inflammatory potency): hydrocortisone 20 mg ≈ prednisone 5 mg ≈ methylprednisolone 4 mg ≈ dexamethasone 0.75 mg; dexamethasone has negligible mineralocorticoid activity.

front: Calc: furosemide 40 mg PO BID and levofloxacin 750 mg IV daily. Convert each route.
bottom: Furosemide 20 mg IV BID; levofloxacin 750 mg PO daily.

bullets.treat: 40 × 0.5 = 20 mg IV. Levofloxacin is about 99% bioavailable: 1:1.
bullets.trap: Separate oral levofloxacin from Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn by at least 2 hours.

back: Furosemide 20 mg IV BID; levofloxacin 750 mg PO daily. Given: Oral furosemide bioavailability is about 50%. Work: 40 × 0.5 = 20 mg IV. Levofloxacin is about 99% bioavailable: 1:1. Exam trap: Separate oral levofloxacin from Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn by at least 2 hours.

diagram.alt: Threshold. Furosemide 20 mg IV BID; levofloxacin 750 mg PO daily.

source.recommendation: Furosemide labeling: oral bioavailability ~50% (range 10–100%), so IV dose is about half the oral dose. Levofloxacin labeling: oral bioavailability ~99%, oral and IV interchangeable; give oral doses at least 2 hours before or after antacids with Mg/Al, sucralfate, metal cations.

topic: Insulin conversions: IV drip to SC basal-bolus; NPH to glargine
front: Calc: NPH 20 units twice daily switching to once-daily glargine. Dose?

bullets.clue: Twice-daily NPH to glargine: reduce total by 20%.
bullets.trap: Drip to SC: give basal insulin about 2 hours before stopping the IV infusion.

back: Glargine 32 units once daily. Given: Twice-daily NPH to glargine: reduce total by 20%. Work: 20 + 20 = 40 units × 0.8 = 32 units. Exam trap: Drip to SC: give basal insulin about 2 hours before stopping the IV infusion.

source.recommendation: Insulin glargine labeling: when switching from twice-daily NPH, the initial glargine dose is 80% of total daily NPH dose. ADA Standards of Care 2026 (Section 16): when transitioning from IV to SC insulin, administer basal insulin 2 h before discontinuing the infusion.

front: Calc: express epinephrine 1:1,000 as % w/v and mg/mL.

bullets.trap: Labels now state mg/mL: 1:10,000 is 0.1 mg/mL. 1 ppm = 0.0001%.

back: 0.1% w/v = 1 mg/mL. Given: Ratio strength 1:1,000 = 1 g in 1,000 mL. Work: 1 g/1,000 mL = 0.1 g/100 mL = 0.1%; = 1,000 mg/1,000 mL = 1 mg/mL. Exam trap: Labels now state mg/mL: 1:10,000 is 0.1 mg/mL. 1 ppm = 0.0001%.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: ratio strength, percentage and ppm calculations. USP labeling standards require single-entity epinephrine injections to express strength in mg/mL rather than ratio.

front: Calc: make 100 mL of 2% solution from a 10% stock. How much stock?

bullets.trap: Diluent is 80 mL, not 100 mL.

back: 20 mL stock + 80 mL diluent. Given: C1V1 = C2V2. Work: 10% × V1 = 2% × 100 mL; V1 = 20 mL. Exam trap: Diluent is 80 mL, not 100 mL.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: dilution and concentration calculations, (quantity1)(concentration1) = (quantity2)(concentration2).

front: Calc: make 100 g of 40% ointment from 70% and 30% stocks. How much of each?

bullets.clue: Alligation: parts of high = 40 − 30 = 10; parts of low = 70 − 40 = 30.
bullets.trap: Parts come from the opposite corner of the grid.

back: 25 g of 70% + 75 g of 30%. Given: Alligation: parts of high = 40 − 30 = 10; parts of low = 70 − 40 = 30. Work: 10/40 × 100 = 25 g; 30/40 × 100 = 75 g. Check: 17.5 + 22.5 = 40 g. Exam trap: Parts come from the opposite corner of the grid.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: alligation alternate for mixing two strengths to obtain an intermediate strength.

front: Calc: how many grams of KCl (MW 74.5) provide 20 mEq?

bullets.clue: mEq = mg × valence ÷ MW; KCl valence 1.
bullets.trap: Divalent ions (Ca, Mg): divide MW by 2 per mEq.

back: 1.49 g KCl. Given: mEq = mg × valence ÷ MW; KCl valence 1. Work: 20 × 74.5 ÷ 1 = 1,490 mg = 1.49 g. Exam trap: Divalent ions (Ca, Mg): divide MW by 2 per mEq.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: milliequivalent calculations, mEq = (mg × valence) / formula weight.

topic: Milliosmoles and osmolarity of IV fluids (NS, D5W)
front: Calc: osmolarity of 0.9% sodium chloride (MW 58.5)?

bullets.trap: Peripheral PN: keep osmolarity ≤900 mOsm/L.

back: About 308 mOsm/L. Given: 0.9% = 9 g/L; NaCl dissociates into 2 particles. Work: 9 ÷ 58.5 = 0.154 mol/L × 2 = 308 mOsm/L. Exam trap: Peripheral PN: keep osmolarity ≤900 mOsm/L.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: mOsmol/L = (g/L ÷ MW) × number of particles × 1000. ASPEN Parenteral Nutrition Safety Consensus Recommendations (2014): peripheral PN osmolarity limit 900 mOsm/L.

front: Calc: 30 mL of a 1% ophthalmic drug (E = 0.18). How much NaCl makes it isotonic?

bullets.trap: E-value = grams NaCl equivalent to 1 g drug.

back: Add 0.216 g NaCl. Given: Isotonic = 0.9% NaCl: 30 mL needs 0.27 g. Work: Drug 0.3 g × 0.18 = 0.054 g NaCl equivalent; 0.27 − 0.054 = 0.216 g. Exam trap: E-value = grams NaCl equivalent to 1 g drug.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: isotonicity calculations using sodium chloride equivalents (E values).

front: Calc: you need 50 g of glycerin (specific gravity 1.25). What volume?

bullets.trap: Multiply for weight, divide for volume.

back: 40 mL. Given: Volume = weight ÷ specific gravity. Work: 50 g ÷ 1.25 g/mL = 40 mL. Exam trap: Multiply for weight, divide for volume.

source.recommendation: USP <1160>: specific gravity relates weight and volume; weight (g) = volume (mL) × specific gravity.

topic: Clinical trial phases, EUA vs full approval, REMS basics
front: A drug gets an Emergency Use Authorization. Is it approved, and where do trial phases fit?

bullets.clue: Phase 1 safety and dosing; 2 efficacy and dose-finding; 3 large confirmatory trials; 4 postmarketing.
bullets.treat: EUA under FD&C Act section 564 during a declared emergency; trials run under an IND (21 CFR 312).
bullets.trap: REMS can be required at or after approval if labeling alone isn't enough.

back: No: EUA is not approval. Key clue: Phase 1 safety and dosing; 2 efficacy and dose-finding; 3 large confirmatory trials; 4 postmarketing. Pharmacist move: EUA under FD&C Act section 564 during a declared emergency; trials run under an IND (21 CFR 312). Exam trap: REMS can be required at or after approval if labeling alone isn't enough.

diagram.alt: Steps. No: EUA is not approval.

source.recommendation: FDA EUA guidance: section 564 authorizes unapproved products or uses during a declared emergency; EUA is distinct from approval. 21 CFR 312.21 describes phases 1–3; phase 4 postmarketing studies. FDAAA 2007 lets FDA require a REMS.

topic: TPN: dextrose, amino acid, lipid kcal and total kcal
front: Calc: PN with dextrose 250 g, amino acids 100 g, 250 mL of 20% lipid. Total kcal?

bullets.clue: Dextrose 3.4 kcal/g; protein 4 kcal/g; 20% lipid 2 kcal/mL.
bullets.trap: Dextrose is 3.4 kcal/g, not 4.

back: 1,750 kcal. Given: Dextrose 3.4 kcal/g; protein 4 kcal/g; 20% lipid 2 kcal/mL. Work: 850 + 400 + 500 = 1,750 kcal. Exam trap: Dextrose is 3.4 kcal/g, not 4.

source.guideline: ASPEN PN Safety Consensus 2014 + ASPEN Safe PN Care Transitions 2022
source.recommendation: ASPEN PN Safety Consensus (2014): energy values used in PN: dextrose monohydrate 3.4 kcal/g, amino acids 4 kcal/g, 20% lipid emulsion 2 kcal/mL (10 kcal/g including glycerol and phospholipid).

topic: TPN nitrogen balance and protein needs (g/kg)
front: Calc: patient gets 100 g protein/day; 24-hour UUN is 12 g. Nitrogen balance?

bullets.trap: Critically ill adults: protein 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day.

back: Balance = 0 (neutral). Given: N intake = protein ÷ 6.25; losses = UUN + 4. Work: 100 ÷ 6.25 = 16 g in; 12 + 4 = 16 g out; balance 0. Exam trap: Critically ill adults: protein 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day.

source.recommendation: ASPEN 2022 adult critical care nutrition guideline: protein 1.2–2.0 g/kg/day; nitrogen balance = (protein g ÷ 6.25) − (UUN + 4) per standard nutrition assessment.

front: Calc: 25 kg child. Holliday-Segar maintenance fluids per day and per hour?

bullets.clue: 100 mL/kg first 10 kg; 50 mL/kg next 10; 20 mL/kg after.
bullets.trap: The 4-2-1 rule gives mL/h, not mL/day.

back: 1,600 mL/day; 65 mL/h. Given: 100 mL/kg first 10 kg; 50 mL/kg next 10; 20 mL/kg after. Work: 1,000 + 500 + 100 = 1,600 mL/day. Hourly 4-2-1: 40 + 20 + 5 = 65 mL/h. Exam trap: The 4-2-1 rule gives mL/h, not mL/day.

source.recommendation: Holliday MA, Segar WE. Pediatrics 1957: maintenance water 100 mL/kg/day for first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for next 10 kg, 20 mL/kg/day thereafter (hourly 4-2-1 mL/kg/h).

topic: NNT, ARR, RRR, OR vs RR
front: Calc: stroke rate 20% on placebo, 15% on drug. ARR, RRR, NNT?

bullets.clue: ARR = control − treatment rate; RRR = ARR ÷ control.
bullets.trap: Round NNT up; RRR looks bigger than ARR.

back: ARR 5%, RRR 25%, NNT 20. Given: ARR = control − treatment rate; RRR = ARR ÷ control. Work: 20 − 15 = 5%; 5 ÷ 20 = 25%; NNT = 1 ÷ 0.05 = 20. Exam trap: Round NNT up; RRR looks bigger than ARR.

diagram.alt: Risk calculation flow: control event rate 20 percent, treatment 15 percent. ARR 5 percent, RRR 25 percent, NNT 20.

source.recommendation: Standard EBM definitions (CEBM): ARR = CER − EER; RRR = (CER − EER)/CER; NNT = 1/ARR rounded up.

front: Calc: TP 90, FN 10, FP 20, TN 180. Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV?

bullets.trap: PPV and NPV shift with prevalence; sensitivity and specificity don't.

back: Sens 90%, spec 90%, PPV 82%, NPV 95%. Given: Sens = TP/(TP+FN); spec = TN/(TN+FP). Work: 90/100 = 90%; 180/200 = 90%; PPV 90/110 = 82%; NPV 180/190 = 95%. Exam trap: PPV and NPV shift with prevalence; sensitivity and specificity don't.

diagram.alt: Two-by-two table: TP 90, FN 10, FP 20, TN 180. Sensitivity 90 over 100 is 90 percent, specificity 180 over 200 is 90 percent, PPV 90 over 110 is 82 percent, NPV 180 over 190 is 95 percent.

source.recommendation: Standard EBM definitions (CEBM): sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values; predictive values depend on prevalence.

topic: Loading & maintenance doses: Vd, Cl, half-life, ke
front: Calc: Vd 0.5 L/kg, 70 kg, target 15 mg/L. Loading dose, and time to steady state without one?

bullets.treat: 0.5 × 70 = 35 L × 15 = 525 mg. Steady state takes 4–5 half-lives; t½ = 0.693 ÷ k.
bullets.trap: Loading dose depends on Vd; maintenance depends on clearance.

back: Loading dose 525 mg. Given: LD = Vd × target concentration (F = 1). Work: 0.5 × 70 = 35 L × 15 = 525 mg. Steady state takes 4–5 half-lives; t½ = 0.693 ÷ k. Exam trap: Loading dose depends on Vd; maintenance depends on clearance.

diagram.alt: Loading dose versus accumulation: without a loading dose, drug reaches 50, 75, 88, 94 and 97 percent of steady state after 1 to 5 half-lives; a loading dose of Vd times target concentration reaches target at once.

source.recommendation: Applied clinical pharmacokinetics (Winter's Basic Clinical Pharmacokinetics): LD = Vd × Css ÷ (S × F); maintenance dose rate = CL × Css; t½ = 0.693/ke; ~4–5 half-lives to reach steady state.

front: Calc: serious MRSA infection, vancomycin CL 4 L/h, AUC target 500. Daily dose?

bullets.trap: Trough-only dosing (15–20) is no longer recommended.

back: 2,000 mg/day. Given: Target AUC 400–600 mg·h/L (MIC 1). Work: Daily dose = AUC × CL = 500 × 4 = 2,000 mg/day. Exam trap: Trough-only dosing (15–20) is no longer recommended.

source.recommendation: ASHP/IDSA/PIDS/SIDP 2020 vancomycin consensus: AUC/MIC 400–600 (assuming MIC 1) for serious MRSA infections, preferably Bayesian-guided; trough-only monitoring targeting 15–20 mg/L no longer recommended. Total daily dose = AUC24 × CL.
